summary.text: Tony Luetkemeyer is the Republican State Senator for Missouri's 34th Senatorial District, representing Buchanan and Platte counties.
He was first elected in November 2018, was reelected in November 2022, and serves as Majority Floor Leader.

paragraphs.text: Luetkemeyer grew up in Farmington in southeast Missouri and attended the University of Missouri, where he was elected student body president.
After college he worked as a White House intern in the Domestic Policy Council under President George W. Bush, then enrolled at the University of Missouri School of Law.

While in law school he was appointed by Governor Matt Blunt to the University of Missouri Board of Curators, and after graduating he clerked for Judge Patricia Breckenridge on the Supreme Court of Missouri.
Before becoming Majority Floor Leader, Luetkemeyer served as Majority Caucus Chairman and Majority Whip, and as chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee.
His Senate biography says he sponsored and passed legislation freezing property taxes on the homes of Missouri seniors and eliminating the income tax on Social Security and other retirement benefits.
He currently practices law in Kansas City, is a member of the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association and the Federalist Society, and resides in Parkville with his wife and their son.
